questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The possessive must agree with the plural noun 'departments', so 'its' must be 'their'. The corrected sentence is: 'The two departments exchanged their data sets under a formal sharing agreement.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) No sooner did the alert appear
(B) on the monitoring dashboard
(C) when the engineer
(D) isolated the affected node.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The correlative of 'no sooner' is 'than', not 'when'. The corrected sentence is: 'No sooner did the alert appear on the monitoring dashboard than the engineer isolated the affected node.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the grammatically incorrect section of the sentence:

(A) She has little friends in the new city,
(B) but she speaks to her family
(C) every evening
(D) over a video call.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Friends' is countable, so the quantifier must be 'few'; 'little' is used with uncountable nouns. The corrected sentence is: 'She has few friends in the new city, but she speaks to her family every evening over a video call.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) The prize
(B) money was distributed
(C) between the five members
(D) of the winning team at the closing ceremony.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. 'Between' is used for two parties; with more than two, 'among' is required. The corrected sentence is: 'The prize money was distributed among the five members of the winning team at the closing ceremony.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the incorrect portion of the sentence:

(A) The committee
(B) has not yet agreed
(C) among themselves
(D) about the revised fee structure.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. When a collective noun is used with 'among themselves', the members are acting individually, so the plural verb form is required: 'have not yet agreed'. The corrected sentence is: 'The committee have not yet agreed among themselves about the revised fee structure.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) The institute plans
(B) on launching
(C) a certificate course in robotics
(D) early next year.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Plan' is followed by a to-infinitive, not by 'on' plus a gerund, so 'on launching' must be 'to launch'. The corrected sentence is: 'The institute plans to launch a certificate course in robotics early next year.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the grammatically incorrect section of the sentence:

(A) Its a well-known fact
(B) that regular backups
(C) reduce the impact
(D) of a ransomware attack.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Its' is possessive; the contraction of 'it is' is 'it's', so the sentence must begin with 'It is a well-known fact'. The corrected sentence is: 'It is a well-known fact that regular backups reduce the impact of a ransomware attack.'

questions.questionText:
Which segment of the sentence needs correction?

(A) Everyone attended the review
(B) accept the two interns
(C) who were on site
(D) at the customer's factory.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Accept' means to receive willingly; the word meaning 'apart from' is 'except'. The corrected sentence is: 'Everyone attended the review except the two interns who were on site at the customer's factory.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) Provided that the funds are released on time,
(B) the construction
(C) can be completed
(D) before the monsoon will arrive.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. A future time clause introduced by 'before' uses the present tense, so 'will arrive' must be 'arrives'. The corrected sentence is: 'Provided that the funds are released on time, the construction can be completed before the monsoon arrives.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) He remembers the day
(B) when he had joined the company,
(C) which was raining heavily
(D) across the entire city.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The relative pronoun 'which' has no suitable antecedent for a weather statement; the clause should begin with 'when it was raining heavily'. The corrected sentence is: 'He remembers the day when he joined the company, when it was raining heavily across the entire city.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) The two candidates were equally good,
(B) so the panel could not decide
(C) which of them was
(D) the more suitable of all the applicants.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. A comparison between two people cannot be extended to 'all the applicants'; the phrase should be 'the more suitable of the two'. The corrected sentence is: 'The two candidates were equally good, so the panel could not decide which of them was the more suitable of the two.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) The clients were impressed
(B) by the demonstration
(C) given by we
(D) three final-year students.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. After the preposition 'by', the objective form is required, so 'we three' must be 'us three'. The corrected sentence is: 'The clients were impressed by the demonstration given by us three final-year students.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) Every of the participants
(B) received a certificate
(C) and a reference book
(D) at the end of the programme.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Every' cannot be followed by 'of'; the correct form is 'each of the participants' or 'every participant'. The corrected sentence is: 'Each of the participants received a certificate and a reference book at the end of the programme.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) Candidates dare not to miss
(B) the document verification,
(C) because late entries
(D) are not permitted at the venue.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. As a modal, 'dare not' is followed by a bare infinitive, so 'dare not to miss' must be 'dare not miss'. The corrected sentence is: 'Candidates dare not miss the document verification, because late entries are not permitted at the venue.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) Not only did the team meet the target
(B) but they also reduced
(C) the defect rate,
(D) which the client appreciating greatly.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. A finite verb is needed in the relative clause, so 'which the client appreciating greatly' must be 'which the client greatly appreciated'. The corrected sentence is: 'Not only did the team meet the target but they also reduced the defect rate, which the client greatly appreciated.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the incorrect portion of the sentence:

(A) The decision depends
(B) on whether the funding
(C) will be approved
(D) till the end of the quarter.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. 'Till' marks a point up to which an action continues, whereas a deadline for completion requires 'by'. The corrected sentence is: 'The decision depends on whether the funding will be approved by the end of the quarter.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) A series of
(B) workshops on cybersecurity
(C) have been planned
(D) for employees of the two regional offices.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The subject is the singular 'a series', not 'workshops', so the verb must be 'has been planned'. The corrected sentence is: 'A series of workshops on cybersecurity has been planned for employees of the two regional offices.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) Before the audit began,
(B) the records
(C) have been arranged
(D) in chronological order.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. An action completed before a past event takes the past perfect passive, so 'have been arranged' must be 'had been arranged'. The corrected sentence is: 'Before the audit began, the records had been arranged in chronological order.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) The principle of the college
(B) inaugurated the innovation lab
(C) in the presence of
(D) several industry representatives.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. The head of a college is the 'principal'; 'principle' means a rule or doctrine. The corrected sentence is: 'The principal of the college inaugurated the innovation lab in the presence of several industry representatives.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) The cost of raw
(B) materials and of transport
(C) have risen
(D) steadily since the new tax came into force.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The subject is the singular 'the cost', even though two sources of cost are mentioned, so 'have risen' must be 'has risen'. The corrected sentence is: 'The cost of raw materials and of transport has risen steadily since the new tax came into force.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) Having completed the safety induction,
(B) the new technicians were allowed to enter the shop floor,
(C) where they worked under close supervision for a week.
(D) No error
questions.explanationText: All the given parts are grammatically correct, so there is no error. The participial phrase correctly modifies 'the new technicians', and the relative adverb 'where' refers properly to the shop floor.

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) The new privacy rules will effect
(B) every user
(C) who has registered
(D) through the mobile application.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Effect' as a verb means 'bring about'; the verb meaning 'influence' is 'affect'. The corrected sentence is: 'The new privacy rules will affect every user who has registered through the mobile application.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) Students needs not bring
(B) their laptops
(C) to the lecture,
(D) as tablets will be provided.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Need not' is a modal and does not take the -s ending, so 'needs not bring' must be 'need not bring'. The corrected sentence is: 'Students need not bring their laptops to the lecture, as tablets will be provided.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) A number of applications
(B) has been rejected
(C) because the candidates
(D) did not meet the eligibility criteria.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'A number of' is followed by a plural verb, unlike 'the number of'; therefore 'has been rejected' must be 'have been rejected'. The corrected sentence is: 'A number of applications have been rejected because the candidates did not meet the eligibility criteria.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) The engineers were testing the turbine
(B) when the power supply
(C) has failed
(D) without any warning.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. A single completed event interrupting a past continuous action takes the simple past, so 'has failed' must be 'failed'. The corrected sentence is: 'The engineers were testing the turbine when the power supply failed without any warning.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) The report mentions several risks,
(B) most of which
(C) has not been
(D) addressed in the mitigation plan.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. 'Most of which' refers to the plural 'risks', so the verb must be 'have not been'. The corrected sentence is: 'The report mentions several risks, most of which have not been addressed in the mitigation plan.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) The output of
(B) the new plant
(C) is twice as higher
(D) as that of the old one, according to the production report.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The 'as ... as' pattern takes the positive degree, so 'as higher as' must be 'as high as'. The corrected sentence is: 'The output of the new plant is twice as high as that of the old one, according to the production report.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) The Ganga is
(B) longest river
(C) in northern India
(D) and supports millions of farmers.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. A superlative requires the definite article, so 'longest river' must be 'the longest river'. The corrected sentence is: 'The Ganga is the longest river in northern India and supports millions of farmers.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) Both the proposals were strong,
(B) but the committee asked
(C) for some more informations
(D) before taking a final decision.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. 'Information' is uncountable and has no plural form, so 'informations' must be 'information'. The corrected sentence is: 'Both the proposals were strong, but the committee asked for some more information before taking a final decision.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) Walking through the laboratory,
(B) the machines appeared
(C) unusually noisy
(D) to the visiting students.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. The participial phrase must modify the people who were walking, but the sentence attaches it to 'the machines', creating a dangling modifier. The corrected sentence is: 'Walking through the laboratory, the visiting students found the machines unusually noisy.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the grammatically incorrect section of the sentence:

(A) His approach is quite different
(B) than the one
(C) recommended in the standard
(D) operating procedure.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. In formal English 'different' is followed by 'from', so 'different than' must be 'different from'. The corrected sentence is: 'His approach is quite different from the one recommended in the standard operating procedure.'

questions.questionText:
Which segment of the sentence needs correction?

(A) The technician
(B) is repairing
(C) the conveyor belt
(D) since Monday afternoon.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. An action that began in the past and continues up to now requires the present perfect continuous, so 'is repairing' must be 'has been repairing'. The corrected sentence is: 'The technician has been repairing the conveyor belt since Monday afternoon.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) Each of the four modules
(B) must be approved
(C) by both the reviewer
(D) and the three domain experts.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. 'Both' refers to two items only, so it cannot introduce a list that includes three experts; 'by the reviewer and the three domain experts' is required. The corrected sentence is: 'Each of the four modules must be approved by the reviewer and the three domain experts.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the grammatically incorrect section of the sentence:

(A) The manager announced
(B) that he would discuss the appraisal
(C) with the employees in his cabin
(D) who had exceeded their targets.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. The relative clause is placed too far from the noun it modifies; it should follow 'the employees'. The corrected sentence is: 'The manager announced that he would discuss the appraisal in his cabin with the employees who had exceeded their targets.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) The supervisor told the trainees
(B) that the plant would remain closed
(C) on the following Monday
(D) and asked them that whether they could work from home.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. A reported yes/no question takes 'whether' alone; 'that whether' is ungrammatical. The corrected sentence is: 'The supervisor told the trainees that the plant would remain closed on the following Monday and asked them whether they could work from home.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) The new policy aims both to reduce paperwork
(B) and improving
(C) the speed of approvals
(D) across all departments.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. With 'both ... and' the two elements must have the same form, so 'improving' must be 'to improve'. The corrected sentence is: 'The new policy aims both to reduce paperwork and to improve the speed of approvals across all departments.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) Both the trainer and the coordinator
(B) was praised
(C) for organising the workshop
(D) at such short notice.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. Two subjects joined by 'both ... and' form a plural subject, so the verb must be 'were praised'. The corrected sentence is: 'Both the trainer and the coordinator were praised for organising the workshop at such short notice.'

questions.questionText:
Which segment of the sentence needs correction?

(A) Hardly had the server been restored
(B) when a second power failure brought the entire facility to a standstill,
(C) forcing the team to switch to the disaster recovery site.
(D) No error
questions.explanationText: All the given parts are grammatically correct, so there is no error. The 'hardly ... when' pattern with inversion and the past perfect is correctly used, and the participial phrase modifies the main clause logically.

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) The report differs
(B) with the earlier version
(C) in three important
(D) respects.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. The verb 'differ' used with a thing takes 'from', so 'differs with' must be 'differs from'. The corrected sentence is: 'The report differs from the earlier version in three important respects.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) After reviewing the
(B) code for three hours,
(C) several defects were discovered
(D) by the quality team in the payment module.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The introductory phrase must modify the people reviewing the code, so the main clause should begin with 'the quality team'. The corrected sentence is: 'After reviewing the code for three hours, the quality team discovered several defects in the payment module.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) Few of the recommendations
(B) was implemented,
(C) which disappointed
(D) the members
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Few of the recommendations' is a plural subject, so the verb must be 'were implemented'. The corrected sentence is: 'Few of the recommendations were implemented, which disappointed the members.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) Please find attached the revised quotation
(B) for the annual maintenance contract,
(C) which includes the service charges
(D) and kindly do the needful as earliest as possible.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. The standard expression is 'as early as possible'; 'as earliest as possible' is not grammatical. The corrected sentence is: 'Please find attached the revised quotation for the annual maintenance contract, which includes the service charges, and kindly respond as early as possible.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) The audit team recommended
(B) that the process
(C) is documented
(D) in detail within a month.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. After 'recommend that', the subjunctive base form is used, so 'is documented' must be 'be documented'. The corrected sentence is: 'The audit team recommended that the process be documented in detail within a month.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the grammatically incorrect section of the sentence:

(A) An honourable mention
(B) was given to team
(C) that built a solar-powered
(D) air quality sensor for the campus.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. A specific team already identified by the relative clause requires the definite article, so 'to team' must be 'to the team'. The corrected sentence is: 'An honourable mention was given to the team that built a solar-powered air quality sensor for the campus.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) She said that she
(B) will complete
(C) the documentation
(D) before the release date.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. After a past reporting verb the future 'will' becomes 'would' in the subordinate clause. The corrected sentence is: 'She said that she would complete the documentation before the release date.'

questions.questionText:
Which segment of the sentence needs correction?

(A) The news about the layoffs
(B) have spread
(C) across the campus
(D) within a few hours.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'News' is an uncountable noun taking a singular verb, so 'have spread' must be 'has spread'. The corrected sentence is: 'The news about the layoffs has spread across the campus within a few hours.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) The machine used to running
(B) continuously for twelve hours
(C) before the new
(D) maintenance schedule was introduced.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Used to' is followed by the base form, so 'used to running' must be 'used to run'. The corrected sentence is: 'The machine used to run continuously for twelve hours before the new maintenance schedule was introduced.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) He is studying
(B) in a engineering college
(C) that was established
(D) nearly fifty years ago.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Engineering' begins with a vowel sound, so the article must be 'an engineering college'. The corrected sentence is: 'He is studying in an engineering college that was established nearly fifty years ago.'

questions.questionText:
Which segment of the sentence needs correction?

(A) To qualify
(B) for the scholarship,
(C) the application must be submitted
(D) with the income certificate before the last date.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The infinitive phrase must refer to the person qualifying, so the main clause should name the applicant. The corrected sentence is: 'To qualify for the scholarship, a candidate must submit the application with the income certificate before the last date.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) She studied hard for the examination
(B) so that she can
(C) secure a place
(D) in the postgraduate programme.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. After a past main clause, the purpose clause takes 'could', so 'can' must be 'could'. The corrected sentence is: 'She studied hard for the examination so that she could secure a place in the postgraduate programme.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the incorrect portion of the sentence:

(A) This is the village
(B) where the solar project
(C) was commissioned,
(D) and which people still depend on firewood.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. The final clause needs an adverbial relative referring to place, so 'which' must be 'where'. The corrected sentence is: 'This is the village where the solar project was commissioned and where people still depend on firewood.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) He avoided
(B) to answer
(C) the question about the missing invoices
(D) during the enquiry.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Avoid' is followed by a gerund, so 'to answer' must be 'answering'. The corrected sentence is: 'He avoided answering the question about the missing invoices during the enquiry.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) Much of the delegates
(B) complained that the sessions
(C) had been scheduled
(D) too close to one another.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Delegates' is a countable plural noun, so the quantifier must be 'many of the delegates'. The corrected sentence is: 'Many of the delegates complained that the sessions had been scheduled too close to one another.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) Covered with dust after the site visit,
(B) the laptop was cleaned
(C) by the intern
(D) before the evening meeting.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. The participial phrase logically describes the laptop, but the structure makes it modify the clause subject in an ambiguous way; the modifier should be attached directly to 'the laptop'. The corrected sentence is: 'The laptop, covered with dust after the site visit, was cleaned by the intern before the evening meeting.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) The intern was accompanied
(B) with his supervisor
(C) when he visited
(D) the client's manufacturing unit.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. A person is accompanied 'by' another person; 'with' is used for things carried. The corrected sentence is: 'The intern was accompanied by his supervisor when he visited the client's manufacturing unit.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) Since more than a decade
(B) the institute has been running
(C) an evening programme
(D) for working professionals.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. A duration requires 'for', so the phrase must be 'For more than a decade'. The corrected sentence is: 'For more than a decade the institute has been running an evening programme for working professionals.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) The speaker repeated the instruction again
(B) because several participants
(C) had not heard it
(D) over the noisy connection.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Repeat' already contains the sense of 'again', making 'repeated again' redundant. The corrected sentence is: 'The speaker repeated the instruction because several participants had not heard it over the noisy connection.'

questions.questionText:
Which segment of the sentence needs correction?

(A) She got down the taxi
(B) at five in the morning
(C) and reached the airport
(D) well before the six o'clock flight.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. One gets 'out of' a car or a taxi; 'got down the taxi' is not idiomatic English. The corrected sentence is: 'She got out of the taxi at five in the morning and reached the airport well before the six o'clock flight.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) Twenty kilometres
(B) are not a long distance
(C) for a cyclist
(D) who trains every morning.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. A measurement treated as one quantity takes a singular verb, so 'are not' must be 'is not'. The corrected sentence is: 'Twenty kilometres is not a long distance for a cyclist who trains every morning.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) The candidate was praised for his clarity of thought,
(B) his technical depth
(C) and because he was punctual
(D) throughout the selection process.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. A noun phrase is needed to match the earlier items, so the third item must be 'his punctuality'. The corrected sentence is: 'The candidate was praised for his clarity of thought, his technical depth and his punctuality throughout the selection process.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) Comparing to last year,
(B) the number of placements
(C) has risen sharply
(D) in the computer science department.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. The correct introductory phrase is 'Compared to last year'. The corrected sentence is: 'Compared to last year, the number of placements has risen sharply in the computer science department.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) He did not remember neither the password
(B) nor the recovery question,
(C) so the account
(D) had to be reset by the administrator.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Neither ... nor' is already negative and cannot follow 'did not'; the phrase should be 'He remembered neither the password'. The corrected sentence is: 'He remembered neither the password nor the recovery question, so the account had to be reset by the administrator.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) The final conclusion of the study
(B) was that remote monitoring
(C) reduces unplanned downtime
(D) in small manufacturing units.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. A conclusion is by definition final, so 'final conclusion' is redundant. The corrected sentence is: 'The conclusion of the study was that remote monitoring reduces unplanned downtime in small manufacturing units.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) The proposal was rejected
(B) not because it lacked technical merit
(C) but on account of its cost,
(D) which the committee feeling was far too high.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. The clause needs a finite verb, so 'which the committee feeling' must be 'which the committee felt'. The corrected sentence is: 'The proposal was rejected not because it lacked technical merit but on account of its cost, which the committee felt was far too high.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the grammatically incorrect section of the sentence:

(A) This is the most unique
(B) solution submitted
(C) to the competition
(D) in the last five years.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Unique' is an absolute adjective and cannot be graded, so 'most unique' is incorrect. The corrected sentence is: 'This is a unique solution submitted to the competition in the last five years.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) Mathematics
(B) are considered
(C) a difficult subject
(D) by many first-year students.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Mathematics' is singular in form and meaning although it ends in -s, so the verb must be 'is considered'. The corrected sentence is: 'Mathematics is considered a difficult subject by many first-year students.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) The researcher who's paper won the award
(B) will deliver
(C) the keynote address
(D) at the conference next month.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. The possessive relative pronoun is 'whose'; 'who's' is the contraction of 'who is'. The corrected sentence is: 'The researcher whose paper won the award will deliver the keynote address at the conference next month.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) The manager congratulated him
(B) for completing
(C) the certification
(D) while handling a full project load.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. The verb 'congratulate' takes the preposition 'on'. The corrected sentence is: 'The manager congratulated him on completing the certification while handling a full project load.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) He drove so fastly
(B) on the highway
(C) that the traffic police
(D) stopped him near the toll plaza.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Fast' is both an adjective and an adverb; the form 'fastly' does not exist. The corrected sentence is: 'He drove so fast on the highway that the traffic police stopped him near the toll plaza.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) She is responsible of
(B) the maintenance
(C) of all the test servers
(D) in the Hyderabad facility.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. The adjective 'responsible' is followed by the preposition 'for', not 'of'. The corrected sentence is: 'She is responsible for the maintenance of all the test servers in the Hyderabad facility.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) He has been interested
(B) on artificial intelligence
(C) ever since he attended
(D) a workshop in his second year.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. The adjective 'interested' takes the preposition 'in'. The corrected sentence is: 'He has been interested in artificial intelligence ever since he attended a workshop in his second year.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) She nearly completed
(B) the whole assignment
(C) but could not submit it
(D) because the portal closed early.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. The adverb 'nearly' should be placed next to the word it modifies; 'nearly completed' suggests she did not finish, while the intended meaning is 'completed nearly the whole assignment'. The corrected sentence is: 'She completed nearly the whole assignment but could not submit it because the portal closed early.'

questions.questionText:
Which segment of the sentence needs correction?

(A) Hardly had the meeting started
(B) when the network
(C) fails
(D) and the call was disconnected.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The 'hardly ... when' pattern requires the simple past in the second clause, so 'fails' must be 'failed'. The corrected sentence is: 'Hardly had the meeting started when the network failed and the call was disconnected.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) The courier promised to return back
(B) the damaged parcel
(C) to the warehouse
(D) by Thursday afternoon.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Return' already means 'come or give back', so 'return back' is redundant. The corrected sentence is: 'The courier promised to return the damaged parcel to the warehouse by Thursday afternoon.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) The manager himself
(B) distributed the certificates
(C) to myself
(D) and the other volunteers.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. A reflexive pronoun cannot serve as the object of a preposition when no earlier reference matches it, so 'myself' must be 'me'. The corrected sentence is: 'The manager himself distributed the certificates to me and the other volunteers.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the incorrect portion of the sentence:

(A) He bought
(B) an uniform
(C) and a pair of shoes
(D) before joining the training academy.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Uniform' begins with the consonant sound /j/, so the article must be 'a uniform'. The corrected sentence is: 'He bought a uniform and a pair of shoes before joining the training academy.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) The poor
(B) needs better access
(C) to public health services
(D) in the remote districts.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'The poor' denotes a plural class of people and therefore takes a plural verb, 'need'. The corrected sentence is: 'The poor need better access to public health services in the remote districts.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) Honesty
(B) is a best policy
(C) that every professional
(D) should follow without exception.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. A superlative adjective takes the definite article, so 'a best policy' must be 'the best policy'. The corrected sentence is: 'Honesty is the best policy that every professional should follow without exception.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) Unless the backup is restored,
(B) the reports
(C) will not be generated
(D) and neither the dashboard will update.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. After 'neither' the auxiliary must precede the subject, so the clause should read 'nor will the dashboard update'. The corrected sentence is: 'Unless the backup is restored, the reports will not be generated, nor will the dashboard update.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) The climate of Bengaluru
(B) is better
(C) than Chennai
(D) for outdoor testing throughout the year.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The comparison must be between comparable items, so the sentence should compare the climate of Bengaluru with that of Chennai. The corrected sentence is: 'The climate of Bengaluru is better than that of Chennai for outdoor testing throughout the year.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the grammatically incorrect section of the sentence:

(A) His handwriting is
(B) worst than
(C) mine, yet the examiner
(D) managed to read every word.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. The comparative form is 'worse'; 'worst' is the superlative and cannot be used with 'than' here. The corrected sentence is: 'His handwriting is worse than mine, yet the examiner managed to read every word.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) The auditors examined the vouchers,
(B) interviewed the store keeper
(C) and inspected the warehouse
(D) which taking nearly the whole day.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. A finite verb is required in the relative clause, so 'which taking' must be 'which took'. The corrected sentence is: 'The auditors examined the vouchers, interviewed the store keeper and inspected the warehouse, which took nearly the whole day.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) Kindly note that the training session
(B) has been rescheduled to Thursday
(C) because of the server upgrade,
(D) and all participants are requested to confirm their attendance in advance before.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. 'In advance' and 'before' convey the same meaning, so using both is redundant. The corrected sentence is: 'Kindly note that the training session has been rescheduled to Thursday because of the server upgrade, and all participants are requested to confirm their attendance in advance.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) The candidate should have
(B) informed the panel
(C) that he can joined
(D) only after two months.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. A modal is followed by the base form, so 'can joined' must be 'could join' in this reported context. The corrected sentence is: 'The candidate should have informed the panel that he could join only after two months.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) Because the testing environment was unavailable
(B) for almost two days,
(C) the release was postponed,
(D) and which annoyed the client considerably.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. A relative pronoun cannot follow the coordinating conjunction in this way; the clause should read 'which annoyed the client considerably'. The corrected sentence is: 'Because the testing environment was unavailable for almost two days, the release was postponed, which annoyed the client considerably.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) Either the configuration file
(B) is corrupted
(C) or the service has not been restarted,
(D) but both cannot be true at once.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. The alternatives have already been presented by 'either ... or', so the added clause is redundant and contradicts the inclusive reading; it should be omitted or rephrased as 'though only one of these can be verified now'. The corrected sentence is: 'Either the configuration file is corrupted or the service has not been restarted, though only one of these can be verified now.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) Please lay the
(B) equipment on the bench
(C) and than connect
(D) the probe to the oscilloscope before switching on the supply.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The conjunction indicating sequence is 'then'; 'than' is used in comparisons. The corrected sentence is: 'Please lay the equipment on the bench and then connect the probe to the oscilloscope before switching on the supply.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the incorrect portion of the sentence:

(A) The report mentions
(B) that the plant produces
(C) only steel pipes,
(D) which the auditors verified only partly only in March.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. The repeated adverb 'only' makes the sentence ungrammatical and ambiguous; a single, correctly placed 'only' is required. The corrected sentence is: 'The report mentions that the plant produces only steel pipes, which the auditors verified in part in March.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) The jury
(B) was divided
(C) in their opinion
(D) about the winning design.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Divided in their opinion' shows the members acting separately, so the collective noun takes the plural verb 'were divided'. The corrected sentence is: 'The jury were divided in their opinion about the winning design.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the grammatically incorrect section of the sentence:

(A) The two teams divided the workload
(B) between themselves
(C) and finished the migration
(D) in schedule.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. The fixed expression for completing work within the planned time is 'on schedule'. The corrected sentence is: 'The two teams divided the workload between themselves and finished the migration on schedule.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) He said that he will can finish
(B) the regression suite
(C) before the release
(D) if the environment stays stable.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. Two modals cannot be used together; the correct form is 'would be able to finish'. The corrected sentence is: 'He said that he would be able to finish the regression suite before the release if the environment stays stable.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) If he practised coding daily,
(B) he will be able
(C) to clear the online assessment
(D) without much difficulty.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. A second conditional requires 'would be able' in the main clause to match the hypothetical 'practised'. The corrected sentence is: 'If he practised coding daily, he would be able to clear the online assessment without much difficulty.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the incorrect portion of the sentence:

(A) Unless you do not submit
(B) the compliance certificate,
(C) the payment cannot be released
(D) by the finance department.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Unless' already carries a negative meaning, so adding 'do not' creates a double negative; it should be 'Unless you submit'. The corrected sentence is: 'Unless you submit the compliance certificate, the payment cannot be released by the finance department.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) The office will remain closed
(B) since Monday to Wednesday
(C) because of the
(D) annual maintenance shutdown.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. A span between two points of time is expressed with 'from ... to', not 'since ... to'. The corrected sentence is: 'The office will remain closed from Monday to Wednesday because of the annual maintenance shutdown.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) Scarcely anyone in the department
(B) objected to the new timings,
(C) and the revised schedule
(D) was not opposed by nobody at the meeting.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. 'Not ... nobody' is a double negative; the clause should read 'was not opposed by anybody'. The corrected sentence is: 'Scarcely anyone in the department objected to the new timings, and the revised schedule was not opposed by anybody at the meeting.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) Neither the project manager
(B) nor the developers
(C) was aware of
(D) the revised client requirement.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, which is the plural 'developers', so 'was' must be 'were'. The corrected sentence is: 'Neither the project manager nor the developers were aware of the revised client requirement.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the incorrect portion of the sentence:

(A) Physics and chemistry
(B) is taught
(C) in the same laboratory block
(D) during the first semester.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. Two distinct subjects joined by 'and' form a plural subject, so the verb must be 'are taught'. The corrected sentence is: 'Physics and chemistry are taught in the same laboratory block during the first semester.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) No other city in the state
(B) has as many start-ups
(C) than this one,
(D) according to the latest survey.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The 'as many ... as' pattern requires 'as', so 'than this one' must be 'as this one'. The corrected sentence is: 'No other city in the state has as many start-ups as this one, according to the latest survey.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) The committee recommended that the proposal be revised
(B) before it is placed before the board,
(C) which is scheduled to meet early next month.
(D) No error
questions.explanationText: All the given parts are grammatically correct, so there is no error. The subjunctive 'be revised' is correct after 'recommended that', and the relative clause agrees with its antecedent.

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) The prototype performed
(B) very good
(C) during the endurance test
(D) conducted last weekend.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'performed', so 'very good' must be 'very well'. The corrected sentence is: 'The prototype performed very well during the endurance test conducted last weekend.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) She gave the task
(B) to whomever
(C) was available
(D) in the operations room.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. The pronoun is the subject of 'was available', so the subjective form 'whoever' is required. The corrected sentence is: 'She gave the task to whoever was available in the operations room.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) He has worked hardly
(B) for the last six months
(C) to clear all
(D) the backlog tickets.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Hardly' means 'scarcely'; the intended adverb of manner is 'hard'. The corrected sentence is: 'He has worked hard for the last six months to clear all the backlog tickets.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) If the prototype had been tested under load,
(B) the overheating problem would have been detected much earlier,
(C) and the launch need not have been postponed.
(D) No error
questions.explanationText: All the given parts are grammatically correct, so there is no error. The third conditional uses the past perfect in the 'if' clause and 'would have' in the main clause, both of which are correctly formed.

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) The staff of the research centre
(B) is divided
(C) over whether the pilot study
(D) should be extended by a year.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Staff' here refers to the members as individuals who hold differing views, so the plural verb 'are divided' is required. The corrected sentence is: 'The staff of the research centre are divided over whether the pilot study should be extended by a year.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) One of the servers
(B) that handles the payment traffic
(C) were restarted
(D) during the maintenance window.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The subject of the main clause is 'one', which is singular, so 'were restarted' must be 'was restarted'. The corrected sentence is: 'One of the servers that handles the payment traffic was restarted during the maintenance window.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the incorrect portion of the sentence:

(A) The trainer explained the basic fundamentals
(B) of network security
(C) to the new recruits
(D) during the induction week.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Fundamentals' already means the basics, so 'basic fundamentals' is redundant. The corrected sentence is: 'The trainer explained the fundamentals of network security to the new recruits during the induction week.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) The results
(B) will have been declared
(C) by the time
(D) the next semester will begin.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. A time clause introduced by 'by the time' does not take 'will'; the present tense is used instead. The corrected sentence is: 'The results will have been declared by the time the next semester begins.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) The new algorithm is
(B) more faster
(C) than the earlier one
(D) on sparse data sets.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. A double comparative is ungrammatical; 'faster' already carries the comparative meaning. The corrected sentence is: 'The new algorithm is faster than the earlier one on sparse data sets.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) The laptop I bought last year
(B) is inferior than
(C) the model my colleague uses
(D) for video editing.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. Adjectives such as 'inferior' and 'superior' are followed by 'to', not 'than'. The corrected sentence is: 'The laptop I bought last year is inferior to the model my colleague uses for video editing.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the grammatically incorrect section of the sentence:

(A) The two proposals are quite similar
(B) to one another
(C) in their approach
(D) but differ in their cost estimates entirely completely.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. 'Entirely' and 'completely' express the same idea, so using both is redundant. The corrected sentence is: 'The two proposals are quite similar to one another in their approach but differ entirely in their cost estimates.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) He goes to the office by a bus
(B) every morning
(C) and returns
(D) by the metro in the evening.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. Means of transport in such expressions take no article, so 'by a bus' must be 'by bus'. The corrected sentence is: 'He goes to the office by bus every morning and returns by the metro in the evening.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the incorrect portion of the sentence:

(A) The committee has recommended
(B) that the procurement process be simplified
(C) and that approvals be digitised,
(D) with a view to reduce the processing time substantially.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. The expression 'with a view to' is followed by a gerund, so 'to reduce' must be 'to reducing'. The corrected sentence is: 'The committee has recommended that the procurement process be simplified and that approvals be digitised, with a view to reducing the processing time substantially.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) He was appointed as
(B) a Chairman
(C) of the newly formed
(D) advisory committee.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. A unique office held by one person at a time takes the definite article, so 'a Chairman' must be 'the Chairman'. The corrected sentence is: 'He was appointed as the Chairman of the newly formed advisory committee.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) The team completed the migration on Saturday,
(B) the client verified the data on Sunday,
(C) and the report was shared on Monday,
(D) everyone was satisfied with the outcome.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. The last clause is joined to the sentence without a conjunction, producing a comma splice; it should begin a new sentence or be linked with 'and'. The corrected sentence is: 'The team completed the migration on Saturday, the client verified the data on Sunday, and the report was shared on Monday. Everyone was satisfied with the outcome.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) He completed
(B) a one-year diploma
(C) in cybersecurity from
(D) an university abroad.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. 'University' begins with a consonant sound, so the correct article is 'a university', not 'an university'. The corrected sentence is: 'He completed a one-year diploma in cybersecurity from a university abroad.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) Either the senior analyst or her assistants
(B) is expected
(C) to present the quarterly findings
(D) to the board.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. With 'either ... or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'assistants', which is plural, so 'is expected' must be 'are expected'. The corrected sentence is: 'Either the senior analyst or her assistants are expected to present the quarterly findings to the board.'

questions.questionText:
Select the part that contains the grammatical error:

(A) The cost of the imported sensor
(B) is three times more higher
(C) than that of the local one,
(D) which surprised the buyers.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Higher' is already a comparative form and cannot follow 'more'; the multiple is expressed as 'three times as high as'. The corrected sentence is: 'The cost of the imported sensor is three times as high as that of the local one, which surprised the buyers.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) The shelf contains many books
(B) on machine learning,
(C) but there is only a few
(D) on quantum computing.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. 'A few' is plural, so the verb must be 'are'. The corrected sentence is: 'The shelf contains many books on machine learning, but there are only a few on quantum computing.'

questions.questionText:
Which segment of the sentence needs correction?

(A) The number of students
(B) opting for data science
(C) have increased
(D) sharply over the last three years.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. 'The number of' is a singular subject and takes a singular verb, so 'have increased' must be 'has increased'. The corrected sentence is: 'The number of students opting for data science has increased sharply over the last three years.'

questions.questionText:
Which segment of the sentence needs correction?

(A) You must to submit
(B) the medical certificate
(C) within a week
(D) of resuming duty.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. A modal verb is followed by the bare infinitive, so 'must to submit' must be 'must submit'. The corrected sentence is: 'You must submit the medical certificate within a week of resuming duty.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) Last year the department
(B) was publishing
(C) four research papers
(D) in reputed international journals.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. A completed, countable achievement in a finished year takes the simple past, so 'was publishing' must be 'published'. The corrected sentence is: 'Last year the department published four research papers in reputed international journals.'

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) She has been offered
(B) the scholarship
(C) by a university in Germany
(D) and an internship in a Japan.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. Names of most countries do not take an article, so 'a Japan' must be 'Japan'. The corrected sentence is: 'She has been offered the scholarship by a university in Germany and an internship in Japan.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) There is hardly no time
(B) left before the submission,
(C) so the team decided
(D) to work through the night.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Hardly' is already negative, so 'hardly no time' is a double negative; it must be 'hardly any time'. The corrected sentence is: 'There is hardly any time left before the submission, so the team decided to work through the night.'

questions.questionText:
Find the erroneous part of the sentence:

(A) Reading technical blogs,
(B) attending webinars
(C) and to solve practice problems
(D) have helped him prepare for placements.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. The third gerund phrase is required for parallel structure, so 'to solve' must be 'solving'. The corrected sentence is: 'Reading technical blogs, attending webinars and solving practice problems have helped him prepare for placements.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) The mentor advised the students
(B) to revise the fundamentals
(C) and to practise mock tests,
(D) and warned them to not neglect communication skills.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. A negative infinitive is formed as 'not to', so 'to not neglect' must be 'not to neglect'. The corrected sentence is: 'The mentor advised the students to revise the fundamentals and to practise mock tests, and warned them not to neglect communication skills.'

questions.questionText:
Which part contains an error in usage?

(A) The reason why the deployment failed
(B) is because the configuration file
(C) had not been updated
(D) on the production server.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'The reason why ... is because' is a redundant construction; it should be 'The reason the deployment failed is that'. The corrected sentence is: 'The reason the deployment failed is that the configuration file had not been updated on the production server.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the incorrect portion of the sentence:

(A) The laboratory has fewer equipment
(B) than the one in the main campus,
(C) though its instruments
(D) are considerably newer.
questions.explanationText: Part A contains the error. 'Equipment' is uncountable and takes 'less', not 'fewer'. The corrected sentence is: 'The laboratory has less equipment than the one in the main campus, though its instruments are considerably newer.'

questions.questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(A) She is one of those engineers who insist
(B) on testing every assumption before the design is frozen,
(C) a habit that has saved the team considerable rework.
(D) No error
questions.explanationText: All the given parts are grammatically correct, so there is no error. In 'one of those engineers who', the relative pronoun refers to the plural noun, so 'insist' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?

(A) I have not read
(B) any technical papers late,
(C) as most of my time
(D) goes into project work.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Late' refers to time; the adverb meaning 'recently' is 'lately'. The corrected sentence is: 'I have not read any technical papers lately, as most of my time goes into project work.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) Visitors are not allowed
(B) to enter the server room
(C) unless they would be
(D) accompanied by an authorised employee.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. A condition about the present requires the simple present, so 'would be' must be 'are'. The corrected sentence is: 'Visitors are not allowed to enter the server room unless they are accompanied by an authorised employee.'

questions.questionText:
Choose the segment that contains the error:

(A) The interview lasted for
(B) a hour
(C) and covered questions
(D) on databases and networks.
questions.explanationText: Part B contains the error. 'Hour' begins with a vowel sound because the 'h' is silent, so the article must be 'an hour'. The corrected sentence is: 'The interview lasted for an hour and covered questions on databases and networks.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) Scarcely had the presentation begun
(B) when the projector failed,
(C) and the speaker continued
(D) without the slides nevertheless.
questions.explanationText: Part D contains the error. 'Nevertheless' is misplaced after 'without the slides' and the sense is already carried by the contrast; the sentence should read 'but the speaker nevertheless continued without the slides'. The corrected sentence is: 'Scarcely had the presentation begun when the projector failed, but the speaker nevertheless continued without the slides.'

questions.questionText:
Find the part that should be corrected:

(A) The new policy will come
(B) into effect
(C) from the first of April
(D) in all the regional branches.
questions.explanationText: Part C contains the error. With a starting point of time the idiom is 'with effect from' or simply 'on'; 'come into effect from' is redundant and should be 'come into effect on the first of April'. The corrected sentence is: 'The new policy will come into effect on the first of April in all the regional branches.'
